comments.text: @Machistmo  This card has 12GB real available at all times for the GPU. Each memory module needs a 32bis channel. In this case, you have six memory modules of 2GB each that have their 32 bits, that's why the card has 192 bus bits (32 bits x 6 memory modules). On the 16GB 7600 XT, you get cheated. Its bus is 128-bit, so you really have 4 channels of 32-bit so effectively you can only use 8GB of VRAM. The trick of that graph, like the one on the 4060TI, is that you have 2 memory modules on each side of the board, but only one is accessible at the same time, so what you really have is an 8GB+8GB card. This is why the 8GB variants tend to perform a little better than the 16GB (8+8) in performance, but for certain productivity jobs those extra 8GB are useful. But they are selling you that it has 16GB, when that is a bit of a lie. For the 16GB to be real, you'd need a 256-bit bus.
